arguments.summary: Mina Okonkwo writes that a two-year sentence for one satirical post fails proportionality.
arguments.reasons: The fictional report says the sentence is not the least restrictive way to answer the stated harm.
arguments.passage: A two-year prison sentence for one satirical post is not proportionate to the harm the statute names.
arguments.legal_authorities: Mentioned only in the fictional report.
arguments.disclaimer_text: The fictional disclaimer says the assessment is the author's and not an institutional determination.
arguments.principle: A criminal sentence for speech must be proportionate to the stated harm.
arguments.application: The fictional sentence is two years for one satirical post.
arguments.public_limitation: The walkthrough report is fictional. This limitation stays visible on the public screen.

arguments.summary: Mina Okonkwo writes that the offense is vague because it turns on 'public unease' without defining it.
arguments.reasons: The fictional report says the phrase leaves charging decisions open-ended.
arguments.passage: The offense is vague because 'public unease' is undefined.
arguments.disclaimer_text: The fictional disclaimer says the assessment is the author's and not an institutional determination.
arguments.principle: An offense must define the conduct it punishes.
arguments.application: The fictional statute uses the undefined phrase 'public unease'.
arguments.public_limitation: Only the vagueness sentence is quoted here. The rest of the page is not reproduced.

arguments.application: The fictional report says necessity was not shown.
